title: scl is rational for a chain missing a simple essential curve
body:
## The statement

Let S be a closed hyperbolic surface and C a chain in pi_1(S). If there is a simple
essential curve gamma on S disjoint from the support of C, then scl(C) is rational.

## The proof, or where to find it

Cut S along gamma. Since C is disjoint from gamma, the computation of scl(C) reduces to a
relative computation in the cut-open surface, whose fundamental group is free. Rationality
of scl in that relative setting is already proved.

The reduction is an instance of a theorem in the chapter on free and surface groups of
Calegari, *scl* (MSJ Memoirs 20, 2009), in the subsection "Injective, extremal, isometric
maps": if G is a finite graph of free groups amalgamated along cyclic subgroups, and
g_1, ..., g_n are conjugate into the free vertex subgroups, then scl is piecewise rational
linear on the span of the g_i inside B_1^H(G), and every rational chain there rationally
bounds an extremal surface.

Cutting S along gamma presents pi_1(S) as exactly such a graph of free groups, amalgamated
over the cyclic subgroup carried by gamma: an amalgam when gamma separates, an HNN
extension when it does not. A chain disjoint from gamma is carried by the complementary
pieces, so its terms are conjugate into the vertex groups and the theorem applies.

The cited record gives the full reference.

This is the main thing known in the direction of the general conjecture, that scl is
rational for every chain in the fundamental group of a closed hyperbolic surface. It is
also what makes the general cut-and-glue approach look plausible: the difficulty in
general is not the cutting, but that an arbitrary chain cannot be made disjoint from a
simple essential curve.
